description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Leon Panetta, former US Defense Secretary and former CIA Director, criticizes Secretary Hegseth's political tone in congressional testimony, arguing lawmakers have a duty to scrutinize defense spending. Kevin Book, Managing Director at ClearView Energy Partners, says oil markets are reacting to "uncertainty" tied to both White House policy and tensions in the Persian Gulf. Chris Swonger, President and CEO of the Distilled Spirits Council & Responsibility.org, says President Donald Trump’s pledge to remove a 10% tariff on UK spirits would “inject vitality” into the industry. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Signs Bill Ending DHS Shutdown | Balance of Power: Late Edition 04/30/2026

author: Catherine Lucey
description: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said American officials discussed a possible “Board of Trade” in a call with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng Thursday, casting it as a tool that could help manage economic ties between the two nations.
title: Greer Discusses ‘Board of Trade’ in Call With China’s He Lifeng

description: Chris Swonger, President and CEO of the Distilled Spirits Council and President and CEO of Responsibility.org, says President Donald Trump’s pledge to remove a 10% tariff on UK spirits would “inject vitality” into the industry, boosting trade and giving producers greater predictability between two “uniquely intertwined” whiskey markets. The President's announcement came following King Charles’s visit to the US, though the tariff rollback has not yet been implemented. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Tariff Cut Would Boost US-UK Whiskey Trade: Swonger

description: Kevin Book, Managing Director at ClearView Energy Partners, says oil markets are reacting to "uncertainty" tied to both White House policy and tensions in the Persian Gulf, as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz pushes crude into triple digits. He warns gasoline prices could rise another 20 to 30 cents and says shortages are already emerging in cooking fuels for Asian importers, with global shortfalls possible within weeks to months. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Expert: Gasoline Could Rise Another 20-30 Cents

description: Leon Panetta, former US Defense Secretary and former CIA Director, criticizes Secretary Hegseth's political tone in congressional testimony, arguing lawmakers have a duty to scrutinize defense spending. He warns the standoff in the Strait of Hormuz is damaging both the Iranian and US economies—driving up oil, food and fertilizer prices. Asked whether additional strikes would move the needle, Panetta says negotiations are "the only way" the conflict will ultimately end. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on the late edition Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: More Bombing Won't Move Iran: Panetta

author: Ellen Milligan
description: King Charles III left Washington with the same goodwill from Donald Trump that greeted him when he arrived three days earlier as the president hailed him as “the greatest king,” adding “we need more people like that in our country.”
title: UK Tempers Hopes of US Reset Despite King’s Royal Charm-Fest

author: David Gura, Rachael Lewis-Krisky
description: When the Supreme Court struck down President Trump’s tariffs, it triggered a $166 billion refund process. On today’s Big Take podcast: the logistics of that payout and how soon businesses can expect relief.
title: How the US Government Plans to Refund Billions in Tariffs

description: When the Supreme Court struck down President Trump’s tariffs, it triggered a $166 billion refund process. On today’s Big Take podcast Bloomberg’s Laura Curtis and David Gura discuss how that’s playing out and why some companies might skip out on refunds altogether.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How US Plans To Refund $166 Billion In Tariff Revenue

author: Gregory Korte
description: President Donald Trump ordered federal agencies to make fixed-price agreements the default vehicle for government purchasing, shifting away from cost-reimbursement contracts that he said can lead to runaway spending.
title: Trump Order Pushes Fixed-Price Contracts in Federal Agencies

description: President Donald Trump says Iran's economy is crashing because of the Strait of Hormuz blockade during remarks to reporters at the White House. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says 'Incredible' Hormuz Blockade Is Working

author: Sherif Tarek
description: President Donald Trump invited Iraq’s prime minister nominee to visit Washington after he forms a new government, as the US seeks to limit Iran’s influence on its neighbor.
title: Trump Invites Iraq Premier-Designate to US, Eyeing Stronger Ties

author: Anthony Capaccio
description: Two top Republican lawmakers voiced fresh concern about the fate of President Donald Trump’s $1.5 trillion defense budget request, acknowledging the tough task they’ll face in passing the full amount given the lack of Democratic support and push back within their own party.
title: GOP Lawmakers Voice Fresh Concern Over Defense Budget Request

author: Skylar Woodhouse
description: President Donald Trump said he was aware Amazon.com Inc. is considering a reboot of his hit reality show The Apprentice, with his eldest son potentially taking on the host role.
title: Trump Says He Heard Amazon Weighing ‘Apprentice’ Reboot With Son

author: Nancy Cook
description: Acting AG Todd Blanche is considered the frontrunner for the job.
title: Trump’s Next Attorney General Likely Will Be One of These Three

description: President Donald Trump said he would be removing some whiskey tariffs following a visit from King Charles III during remarks to reporters at the White House.
title: Trump Says He Is Lifting Some Scotch Tariffs

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump indicated he was open to drawing down American military personnel from other NATO members a day after saying he was reviewing US troop levels in Germany.
title: Trump Says He’s Open to Reducing US Troops in Spain, Italy

description: On today's episode on Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Mary Ann Bartels, Sanctuary Wealth Chief Investment Strategist about tech earnings and the S&P500 hitting a record, and  Kate Gulliver, Wayfair CFO on earnings. They also spoke with Dr. Fanny Elahi, Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai Associate Professor of Neurology and Neuroscience. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: S&P Hits Records, Wayfair Earnings Miss | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 4/30/2026

description: "I don’t care. If he stays on he stays on,” President Donald Trump says when asked about his thoughts on Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s decision to stay on the Fed Board of Governors after his term as chair is over. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says He Doesn't Care If Powell Stays on Fed Board

author: Josh Wingrove, Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump said he did not care if the Federal Reserve’s Jay Powell remained as a governor after his tenure as the central bank’s chair ends.
title: Trump Says He Doesn’t Care If Powell Remains on Fed Board

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Josh Wingrove
description: US President Donald Trump on Thursday signed a presidential permit authorizing Bridger Pipeline’s project meant to carry Canadian crude to Wyoming — the latest in years of back-and-forth over oil pipelines linking the countries.
title: Trump Signs Permit for Pipeline from Canada Echoing Keystone XL

description: President Donald Trump says that every American will be able to open a new low-cost IRA account at TrumpIRA.gov, and low-income Americans will be eligible to receive up to $1,000 per year in matching funds. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Signs Order Expanding Access to Retirement Plans

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power,  Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the House vote to end the longest partial government shutdown in US history and provide funding to most of the Department of Homeland Security. On today's show, Republican Senator Steve Daines from Montana, Founder and CEO of Echo Canyon Consulting Jon Seaton, Former Special Assistant to President Biden and Democratic Strategist Meghan Hays, and Chatham House Associate Fellow Natasha Hall (Source: Bloomberg)
title: House Votes to End DHS Shutdown | Balance of Power: Early Edition 4/30/2026

author: Catherine Lucey
description: The US Trade Representative identified Vietnam as a top concern in a new report on intellectual property rights, in a move that could prompt a fresh trade investigation into a leading trading partner.
title: US Names Vietnam as ‘Priority’ Nation on IP Rights Watch List

author: Laura Nahmias
description: Luxury second homes in New York will have to be taxed at a “significant” amount to generate the $500 million of revenue the city is counting on to help close a gaping budget hole, according to a new study from New York City Comptroller Mark Levine’s office.
title: NY Pied-à-Terre Tax Needs Significant Rates to Earn $500 Million

author: Steven T. Dennis
description: The US Senate voted unanimously Thursday to ban its members and staff from trading on fast-growing prediction markets, highlighting concerns about insider trading on the platforms after a US soldier was accused of using classified information to profit from trades.
title: US Senate Bans Members, Staff From Trading on Prediction Markets

author: Franco Dantas, Daniel Carvalho
description: Brazilian lawmakers voted to override President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s veto of a bill to reduce Jair Bolsonaro’s prison sentence, dealing another major blow to the leftist leader ahead of his reelection bid this year.
title: Brazil Congress Shortens Bolsonaro Sentence in Defeat for Lula

author: Jamie Tarabay, Roxana Tiron, Jen Judson
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the US doesn’t let artificial intelligence make lethal targeting decisions even as he called Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei an “ideological lunatic” after a recent spat over military use of the company’s chatbot.
title: Hegseth Calls Anthropic CEO a ‘Lunatic,’ Defends Pentagon AI Use

author: Kate Sullivan
description: US President Donald Trump said he would be removing some whiskey tariffs following a visit from King Charles III, a move that delivers a major trade concession to the United Kingdom.
title: Trump Says He’ll Nix Some Whiskey Tariffs After UK King’s Visit

author: Brian Platt
description: The Alberta government believes it will have Indigenous support for its plan to build a new oil pipeline to the Pacific coast when it’s unveiled in June.
title: Alberta Energy Minister Believes New Pipeline Will Have Indigenous Support

description: Iran’s new supreme leader pledged to not give up the country’s nuclear or missile technologies in a rare statement on Thursday and signaled Tehran would keep control of the Strait of Hormuz. Tyler Kendall reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran’s New Supreme Leader Vows to ‘Guard’ Nuclear Tech

description: President Donald Trump named Nicole Saphier, a radiologist to be US surgeon general after pulling the nomination of wellness entrepreneur Casey Means. The reversal is the second time Trump has withdrawn a pick for role of the nation’s top doctor. Tyler Kendall reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Taps Saphier for Surgeon General After Pulling Means Nomination

author: Kate Sullivan
description: President Donald Trump said Tennessee will redraw its House congressional map following a key Supreme Court decision Wednesday, a move expected to bolster Republicans ahead of what are forecast to be tough midterm elections in November.
title: Trump Says Tennessee to Redraw District Maps to Boost GOP

author: Miranda Davis
description: Trump administration officials enabled misconduct by federal immigration and border patrol agents as part of an enforcement crackdown last year in Chicago, which led to mass raids, many arrests and some violent conflicts with protesters, according to an Illinois state investigation.
title: ICE Misconduct in Chicago Enabled by Trump Officials, State Says

author: Nduka Orjinmo
description: Nigeria’s Supreme Court overturned a ruling that could have derailed the nation’s major opposition party ahead of national elections in 2027.
title: Nigerian Court Clears Path for Unified-Opposition Vote Challenge

author: Khine Lin Kyaw
description: Myanmar’s military-backed government announced Thursday that Aung San Suu Kyi will be moved to house arrest from Naypyidaw Prison to serve her remaining prison term, a conciliatory gesture a few days ahead of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit in the Philippines as the regime seeks international recognition.
title: Myanmar Junta Moves Ex-Leader Aung San Suu Kyi to House Arrest

author: Erik Wasson
description: The longest partial shutdown in US history is nearing an end as the House on Thursday passed funding for most of the Homeland Security Department, just days ahead of missed paychecks for Transportation Security Administration workers that threatened to throw airports into chaos.
title: House Votes to End DHS Shutdown as Threats of Airport Chaos Loom

author: Chris Strohm
description: The US Justice Department plans to file an appeal by Monday against a federal judge’s ruling that blocked prosecutors from using grand jury subpoenas during their investigation into building-cost overruns by the Federal Reserve.
title: DOJ Readies Fed Subpoena Appeal After Closing Powell Probe

author: Rachel Cohrs Zhang, Madison Muller, Jessica Nix
description: President Donald Trump pulled the nomination of wellness entrepreneur Casey Means to be US surgeon general and named Nicole Saphier, a radiologist, to replace her.
title: Trump Nominates Saphier for Surgeon General After Pulling Means

author: Prejula Prem
description: A Pakistani tanker carrying a cargo of diesel from Kuwait appeared to be making an outbound transit through the Strait of Hormuz, a rare event in the blockaded waterway.
title: Pakistani Fuel Tanker Attempts Hormuz Exit Amid Gulf Gridlock

author: Jessica Nix, Ashleigh Furlong
description: AstraZeneca Plc failed to persuade a US regulatory review panel about the benefits of its novel breast cancer medicine, throwing a hurdle in front of a key drug in the company’s pipeline.
title: FDA Panel Votes Against Benefit of Astra’s Breast Cancer Drug

author: Emily Birnbaum
description: A powerful Senate committee backed legislation to require OpenAI, Meta Platforms Inc. and other artificial intelligence companies to stop minors from using chatbots, responding to a strengthening public backlash against harm to children and teenagers attributed to the fast-spreading technology.
title: OpenAI, Meta Targeted in AI Child Safety Bill Senate Panel Backs

description:
The US is seeking to deploy its hypersonic missile for the first time, for possible use against Iran.

Gerry Doyle explains what Dark Eagle is — and why Russia and China are watching. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Seeks to Deploy Hypersonic Missile for the First Time Against Iran

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union’s biggest economies are unhappy with a US proposal to resolve a metals tariff dispute, injecting fresh uncertainty into final negotiations to implement a stalled trade deal.
title: EU Rejects US Plan to End Metals Tariff Spat and Mulls Response

author: Benjamin Penn
description: The Justice Department is pursuing additional charges against James Comey for allegedly leaking classified information, after the former FBI director’s unrelated indictment this week in North Carolina, said two people familiar with the matter.
title: Trump DOJ Pursuing Separate Comey Investigation for Classified Leaks

author: Jorge Valero
description: Euro-area finance ministers will discuss the challenges that Anthropic PBC’s Mythos AI model poses as officials struggle to get clarity on the new tool’s powers.
title: Euro-Area Finance Chiefs to Discuss Mythos as Concerns Mount

author: Felix Tam, Foster Wong
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio spoke with his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi about the Iran war and an upcoming leaders’ summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, China’s state Xinhua News Agency reported on Thursday.
title: Chinese Officials Speak to Bessent, Rubio About Taiwan, Trade

author: Alaric Nightingale
description: Ukraine’s attacks on Russian oil infrastructure climbed to the highest monthly level since December, cutting the neighboring nation’s refinery runs to multi-year lows.
title: Ukraine Strikes on Russian Oil Assets Climb to Four-Month High

author: Annie Massa
description: The US Air Force agreed to buy an undisclosed number of interceptor drones from a company backed by President Donald Trump’s sons, according to the firm, deepening the military’s ties to defense contractors linked to the first family as the US war with Iran enters its third month.
title: Trump Family-Backed Drone Firm Signs Weapons Deal With US

description: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said the market reaction to the central bank's decision to keep interest rates unchanged has been "very sensible," adding that recent UK market moves have so far been "dominated" by the situation in the Middle East, rather than internal political developments. He was speaking in an interview with Bloomberg's Francine Lacqua.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: BOE's Bailey Says Market Reaction to Rates Decision Is 'Sensible'

author: Jamie Tarabay, Roxana Tiron
description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is “causing lasting harm to the military,” the Senate Armed Services Committee’s top Democrat said as the panel hosted the Pentagon chief for a second day of Congressional testimony.
title: Hegseth ‘Causing Lasting Harm’ to Military, Top Democrat Says

author: Prejula Prem, Julian Lee
description: A few Iran-linked vessels are making their way through the Strait of Hormuz, as the crucial waterway remains effectively closed to most international shipping amid blockades by both Tehran and the US.
title: Only Iran-Linked Traffic Moves Through Hormuz Amid Blockades

author: Antony Sguazzin
description: South Africa’s Democratic Alliance party has extolled the need to adopt modern technology to boost government efficiency since joining the ruling coalition as the second-biggest party in 2024.
title: AI Hallucinations Put South African Ministers on the Spot

description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said she knows where, directionally, the central bank is headed. She also added the ramp-up in oil and natural gas costs is not yet triggering so-called "second-round effects." Lagarde was speaking to reporters at a press conference following the ECB's decision to keep rates unchanged. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lagarde Says She Knows Where ECB Is Headed on Rates

author: Maria Paula Mijares Torres
description: The US Attorney for the District of Columbia, Jeanine Pirro, said she will issue more charges against the alleged shooter at a press dinner gala over the weekend.
title: White House Press Dinner Shooting Suspect to Face More Charges, Pirro Says

author: Eric Martin
description: American Airlines Group Inc. resumed flights to Venezuela after a seven-year hiatus, as President Donald Trump pushes to restore commercial and diplomatic ties after ordering the capture of President Nicolas Maduro.
title: American Flight Heads to Caracas as Commercial Flights to Venezuela Resume

description: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett says productivity gains should help keep core prices under control and it would be a mistake for the Federal Reserve and ECB to hike rates during what he sees as a temporary oil shock. Speaking on "Bloomberg Surveillance," Hassett also weighs in on Fed Chair Jerome Powell's plans to stay on at the central bank once his term as chairman ends. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Hassett on Powell Staying at Fed, Inflation and Oil Spike

author: Zoe Tillman
description: Police officers and Democratic lawmakers suing to hold Donald Trump liable for violent riots at the US Capitol more than five years ago face a new round of delays as the president continues to press for immunity against their claims.
title: Trump Seeks Delays in Jan. 6 Civil Suits During Immunity Appeal

description: Two conservative ideas are behind the Supreme Court’s decision to gut the Voting Rights Act. Bloomberg Opinion columnist and Harvard Law professor Noah Feldman explains. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: How the Supreme Court Gutted the Voting Rights Act

description: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett says productivity gains will help keep core prices under control during an interview on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: NEC's Hassett Says a Rate Hike Would Be a Mistake Right Now

author: Craig Stirling, Daniel Hornak
description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said stagflation is a label that belongs to the 1970s and shouldn’t be used to describe the current predicament of the euro zone.
title: Lagarde Joins Powell in Rejecting Stagflation Label of 1970s

author: Ilya Arkhipov, Jon Herskovitz, Soo-Hyang Choi
description: Russia’s war in Ukraine might have taken a different turn without the involvement of North Korea. The weaponry and troops provided by Kim Jong Un’s regime have supported the yearslong bombardment of Ukrainian towns and cities, and also helped repel a surprise Ukrainian incursion into Russian territory in 2024.
title: How North Korea Is Supporting Putin’s War in Ukraine

author: Alberto Nardelli
description: Russia is importing more than 90% of its sanctioned technology through China, a sign of Moscow’s growing reliance on Beijing as Vladimir Putin’s war against Ukraine drags on.
title: Russia Increases Reliance on China for Critical War Technologies

description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde says the euro-area economy is "certainly moving away" from the ECB's baseline scenario, and that policymakers discussed options including a possible rate hike during meetings in Frankfurt. She made the comments at a news conference after officials left the deposit rate at 2%, where it’s been since June 2025. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Lagarde Says ECB Debated Options Including Rate Hike

description: European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said the euro-area economic outlook is “highly uncertain” and will depend on how the war in the Middle East, and its impact on global supply chains, unfolds. Lagarde was speaking to reporters at a press conference following the ECB’s decision to keep interest rates unchanged.
title: ECB’s Lagarde Says Economic Outlook ‘Highly Uncertain’

author: Greg Ryan, Magan Crane
description: Maine Governor Janet Mills suspended her campaign for a US Senate seat on Thursday, upending the race to unseat incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins.
title: Democratic Maine Governor Mills Drops Out of Key Senate Race

author: Milda Seputyte
description: Lithuania’s president said his country should join a US-led naval mission in the Strait of Hormuz in a show of solidarity with Washington.
title: Lithuania Prepares to Join US-Led Mission in Strait of Hormuz

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump will sign an executive order aimed at expanding access to retirement plans for workers whose employers don’t offer that benefit, according to a White House official, a bid to refocus the administration’s messaging on economic issues.
title: Trump to Sign Order to Expand Access to Retirement Plans

description: Kevin Brady, a longtime Republican US House member from Texas, discusses the state's economy, corporate headquarters relocations and the current mood in Congress. He speaks with Bloomberg's Julie Fine. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Ex-Lawmaker Brady Takes Stock of the Texas Economy

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: Unusual bets and outright cheating are drawing scrutiny from firms and regulators
title: Prediction Markets Are Putting Government to the Test

author: Alex Morales
description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer pressed law enforcement authorities to crack down on antisemitic violence, after a stabbing in north London raised fresh questions about the government’s attention to the threats to Britain’s Jewish community.
title: UK to Fast-Track Terrorism Law After Wave of Antisemetic Attacks

author: Patrick Sykes
description: Iran’s record internet blackout is emerging as a key dividing line between the country’s powerful security apparatus and its civilian government, underlining how the war with the US has extended the military’s control over daily life.
title: Iran Internet Blackout Tightens Military’s Grip on Civilian Life

author: Bonolo Mokonoto
description: South Africa will hold local-government elections on Nov. 4, President Cyril Ramaphosa said on Thursday during an televised event near Johannesburg.
title: South Africa to Hold Municipal Elections on November 4

author: Samy Adghirni
description: President Emmanuel Macron appointed his ambassador to Australia as his new chief of staff, replacing Emmanuel Moulin and paving the way for his close ally to be nominated to head the central bank.
title: Macron Taps Ex-Aide Imbert as Chief of Staff After Moulin Exit

author: Bastian Benrath-Wright, Levin Stamm, Paula Doenecke
description: The growing prominence of far-right political parties in Europe is pressuring governments to introduce stricter controls on immigration. Switzerland is set to vote on a proposal that would take things to the next level: capping its population at 10 million.
title: Why Switzerland Is Weighing a 10 Million Population Cap

author: Yian Lee, Stephen Engle, Miaojung Lin
description: The head of Taiwan’s main opposition party said she has asked to meet with President Donald Trump on a planned trip to the US, casting herself as a leader who could prevent a conflict with China through dialogue with the world’s largest economies.
title: Taiwan Opposition Chief Eyes Trump Meeting After Rare Xi Sitdown

description: The European Central Bank headquarters in Frankfurt. Photographer: KIRILL KUDRYAVTSEV/AFP
title: ECB Set to Hold Rates as Officials Assess Iran War Impact

author: Volodymyr Verbianyi
description: Ukraine is in limbo waiting for a resumption of peace talks that might end the war with Russia, with the distraction caused by the conflict in Iran a key obstacle, according to President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
title: Zelenskiy Says Iran War Leaves Ukraine Hanging for Peace Talks

author: Nduka Orjinmo
description: Nigeria’s president named a former Dangote Cement Plc executive as the next head of the nation’s petroleum-products regulator, the third leadership change in four months at the agency that’s clashed with billionaire investor Aliko Dangote.
title: Nigeria Taps Ex-Dangote Exec to Head Oil Regulator After Tension

author: Anthony Cormier, David Kocieniewski
description: Two Democratic senators have asked US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and the cryptocurrency giant Tether for information about a loan between the company and a trust benefitting Lutnick’s children.
title: Two US Senators Seek Cantor Loan Documents From Lutnick and Tether

author: Fiona MacDonald
description: Saudi-UAE tensions are reshaping a volatile region.
title: The UAE Spurs the Gulf’s Regional Realignment

description: The mayor of Kansas City, Missouri, Quinton Lucas says he's trying to ensure that the upcoming World Cup, which is being jointly hosted by the United States, Mexico and Canada, leaves a lasting legacy. Kansas City is hosting six matches, including a quarter-final, and will also be the base for four teams, including both defending champions Argentina and England. On the political front, Lucas ruled out running for Congress for now, and said the Democrats should focus on "affordability and competent governance" in the next election cycle. He spoke with Bloomberg on the sidelines of the Bloomberg CityLab event in Madrid. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Kansas City Mayor on World Cup, US Politics

author: Dana Khraiche
description: Officials in the United Arab Emirates have framed their decision to quit the OPEC group of oil producing nations as an opportunity to respond more nimbly to the energy crisis caused by the Iran war.
title: Why the UAE and Saudi Arabia Have Drifted Apart

author: Alberto Nardelli, Jorge Valero, Olesia Safronova
description: Incoming Hungarian leader Peter Magyar wants to see more rights granted to his country’s minority group in Ukraine before approving Kyiv’s formal negotiations to join the European Union, according to people familiar with the matter.
title: Magyar Wants Help for Ukraine’s Hungarians Before Backing EU Bid

author: Matthew Malinowski
description: Chileans are more concerned about inflation than both security and migration for the first time since at least 2024, according to a new poll that serves as a warning for President José Antonio Kast after he raised fuel costs.
title: Chileans Worry More About Inflation Than Violence After Kast Hikes Fuel Prices

author: Alex Vasquez
description: President Claudia Sheinbaum’s approval rating dipped to its lowest point in April while around half of Mexicans rate the economy as poor, according to a poll published on Thursday.
title: Sheinbaum Approval Hits Lowest Level as Economic Concerns Mount

author: Andreina Itriago
description: Disapproval of interim President Delcy Rodríguez rose in April as Venezuelans grow increasingly impatient with a bleak economic outlook, underscoring mounting pressure on her government following Nicolás Maduro’s January capture.
title: Venezuela Leader’s Approval Falls Amid Economic Gloom

author: Omar Tamo, Eltaf Najafizada
description: The US and Iran showed little sign of breaking their impasse and agreeing to another round of peace talks, with President Donald Trump insisting that his navy’s blockade is working.
title: US and Iran Stuck in Standoff as Oil Prices Soar to Wartime High

author: Sara Sjolin
description: US special envoy to Greenland Jeff Landry is set to embark on his first trip to the Arctic island next month as tensions between Washington and Copenhagen remain strained.
title: Trump’s Greenland Envoy Landry to Make First Visit to Nuuk

author: William Horobin
description: Emmanuel Macron’s chief of staff will leave next week, suggesting the French president is about to nominate a close ally to run the central bank.
title: Macron Moves to Name Top Ally Moulin to Lead Bank of France

description: US President Donald Trump is set to receive a briefing on new military options for action in Iran, signaling the potential for fresh escalation in the Middle East. US Central Command’s Admiral Brad Cooper will meet Trump on Thursday, according to an Axios report, which cited two unnamed people. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US Eyes Fresh Iran Military Options: Report

author: Gonzalo Soto, Michael O'Boyle
description: Less than two years into a presidency rocked by Donald Trump’s unpredictable moves, Mexican leader Claudia Sheinbaum is facing her toughest choice yet in relations with the US.
title: Mexican Governor’s Indictment in US Puts Claudia Sheinbaum in a Bind

description: Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham discusses the role of cities in pushing back against divisive politics, the upcoming UK local elections, and Keir Starmer’s leadership. Burnham spoke to Bloomberg from the 12th Bloomberg CityLab Summit in Madrid. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Andy Burnham on Role of Cities, Local Elections, Political Ambitions

author: Erik Wasson
description: The record-breaking 74-day shutdown of the Department of Homeland Security is nearing an end after House Speaker Mike Johnson united his fractious Republicans behind a two-part budget plan aimed at fully funding the department.
title: DHS Shutdown Nears End as House Approves Republican Budget Plan

description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Michael Allen, Managing Director of Beacon Global Strategies and former Special Assistant to President George W. Bush, says the US should "give it time" for a Strait of Hormuz blockade to pressure Iran economically. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) and Senator Bernie Moreno (R-OH) discuss their bipartisan Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026, warning Chinese-made cars pose a "driving surveillance package" risk and could enable espionage or even remote vehicle takeovers. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fed Keeps Rates Steady As Powell's Leadership Nears End | Balance of Power: Late Edition 04/29/2026
